item.title: Leitrim barber jailed for eight years for rape of woman
item.description: A Leitrim barber has been jailed for eight years for the rape of a woman who was a guest in his home. Dilzar Hamad (40) of Oaklands, Carrick on Shannon, Co Leitrim, was convicted by a jury last year of rape of the woman on a date in January or February 2021. He has no previous convictions. Advertisement The woman told the court in her victim impact statement that following the rape she no longer feels safe. She said the offence and its aftermath has changed her life and the person she is forever

item.title: Local families to benefit from new-born baby grant
item.description: Over 1000 families in the Shannonside region have availed of the new-born baby grant. Minister for Social Protection, Dara Calleary released the figures this week. Budget 2025 introduces a once-off €280 Newborn Baby Grant to help families cover the material needs of a new-born or newly adopted child. Advertisement The grant supports the Government’s First 5 strategy, which focuses on improving outcomes for young children and families. It is paid automatically with the first Child Benefit payment

item.title: Overcrowding continues at local hospitals
item.description: A local hospital is the third busiest in the country as overcrowding continues nationally. That's according to the latest figures released by the Irish Nurses and Midwives Organisation. Sligo University Hospital have 59 admitted patients waiting on beds with only University Hospital Limerick and University Hospital Galway having more patients on trolleys. item.title: Local TD Calls on Bord Bia Chairperson to Resign
item.description: A local TD has called on the chairperson of Bord Bia to resign. The comments come after Dawn Farms, a leading meat supplier, confirmed that Brazilian beef accounted for 1 per cent of its overall beef supply in 2025. Its CEO Larry Murrin is also the Chairman of Bord Bia, whose remit is to market and promote Irish food and drink. item.title: Calls intensify for additional special-education class at Ballyforan National School
item.description: Calls are intensifying for the establishment of an additional special-education class at Ballyforan National School. Families have expressed increasing concern that the current level of provision is insufficient to meet the needs of children requiring autism-specific placements. Classes are currently taking place at the nearby community hall, owned by the local GAA club, St. Aidan's while the roof of the school is said to be in a state of disrepair.
